items.summary: NANOROBOT-ENHANCED DIGITAL TWINS OF BRAIN STATE AT THE LIMIT A multiscale, uncertainty-aware research atlas on microrobotic observations, neural inverse problems, active model discrimination and the limits of computational brain twins. This research monograph asks whether additional microscale observations or strictly bounded reversible experiments can distinguish competing neural-state models that explain conventional measurements equally well. The twin is explicitly defined as a versioned scientific belief, not a digital person, a mind reader or a clinically validated instrument. Its objective is not maximum model complexity but improved identifiability, calibrated prediction under new conditions and faithful retention of failed hypotheses. The work develops five layers: multiscale neural and microenvironment state representation; posterior equivalence and prior sensitivity; non-clinical safe experimental design; frozen-version forking, rollback and reference ancestry; and blind prospective validation against classical state-space systems and independently specified alternatives. Its research architecture includes 30 distinct mathematical derivation plates linked to later chapters, 82 chapters with five independently paginated research sections apiece, 200 detailed Research Gates and 33 revisable Phoenix Answer Embryos. A DOI evidence ledger identifies existing support for brain modeling, latent neural dynamics, experiment design and preclinical microrobot tracking while preventing those sources from being mistaken for evidence of the proposed integrated system. Key research questions include: Can two equally accurate virtual brains be separated by a small, permissible observation? How can the effect of a measurement itself be separated from neural change? When does a prior dominate the inferred brain state? Can the model predict unseen function rather than reconstruct a training signal? Can another laboratory reproduce a rejected twin and safely return to an earlier version? SCIENTIFIC STATUS AND LIMITATIONS This is a forward-looking, non-clinical research synthesis and experimental hypothesis architecture. It provides no personal medical advice, patient-specific interpretations or instruction to deliver neural interventions. Existing murine microrobot tracking and virtual-brain modeling studies do not establish autonomous neural nanorobot readout, human safety, privacy-sensitive mind inference or therapeutic efficacy. Proposed formulas, experiments, research gates and answer embryos are not newly validated biological laws or executed experiments. The work keeps independent safety vetoes, privacy, external reproducibility and explicit model retirement as first-class constraints. Research questions remain open to refutation, correction and reconstruction by future human and AI researchers.

items.summary: Fisher information metric tensors for the 41 held-out SONICOM test subjects, as used in “Evaluating Spatial Discriminability Preservation in HRTF Upsampling Using Fisher Information” (D. Bassett). Code and reproduction instructions: https://github.com/domfrbassett/fisher-rao-hrtf-upsampling What the tensors are At each of the 793 directions of the SONICOM grid, the 2×2 tensor g = JᵀΣ⁻¹J describes how well the auditory cues separate that direction from its neighbours. J is the spatial Jacobian of the cues: Barumerli monaural PGE features, ILD and MaxIACCe-transformed ITD, each fitted with real spherical harmonics. Σ holds the cue noise (σ_mon = 1.25 dB, σ_ILD = 1 dB, σ_ITD = 0.569). All fields are low-pass filtered at 16 kHz before the cues are extracted. The tensor is expressed in a local tangent basis u₁ = a × r, u₂ = r × u₁, where a = z, or y when |r_z| > 0.9, and its units are d′² per rad². Contents metric_tensors.zip has one folder per subject, metric_tensors/subject_####/ , containing 25 files per subject (1,025 in total): reference_metric_tensor.mat : the dense measured HRTF. <METHOD>_N###_metric_tensor.mat : one file per reconstruction. There are six methods: SUpDEq_SH , SUpDEq_MCA , SUpDEq_NN_MCA_6dB (SUpDEq-Natural-MCA in the paper), SUpDEq_Bary_MCA_6dB , RANF and FSP_AE . Each is reconstructed from N = 100, 19, 5 and 3 retained directions. The 164 natural-neighbour and barycentric files at N = 5 and 3 have status “ not_applicable ”. The interpolation is undefined for those masks, so these files carry no tensors. Variables in each file: metricTensor : the tensors at SH order 6 [2×2×793]. familyGram : per-cue-family Gram matrices JᵀJ before noise weighting, at SH orders 4, 6 and 8 [2×2×793×3 families×3 orders]. They let you recompute the tensors with other noise values or SH orders. In reconstruction files only: crossFamilyGram : the unsymmetrised cross terms J_refᵀ J_recon, same layout as familyGram . airmByDirection : the pointwise AIRM discrepancy from the reference. Metadata: coordinates (Cartesian and azimuth/elevation in degrees), cue band, noise values (reference files only), status (“ completed ” or “ not_applicable ”) and, for not-applicable files, a message giving the reason. SHA256SUMS.txt lists a checksum for every file. Format and use The files are MATLAB v7.3 (HDF5), so MATLAB, h5py or any HDF5 reader can open them. Note that h5py reverses MATLAB’s axis order. scripts/fisher_lib.py in the repository reads them and recomputes tensors, AIRM and thresholds from the Gram matrices. To rerun the analysis scripts, unzip into results/evaluation/ so the subject folders sit in results/evaluation/metric_tensors/ . Provenance Produced with run_evaluation("tensors") from the repository above. The values are numerically identical to the tensor files behind results/evaluation/full_evaluation_summary.csv ; this run additionally stores the cross terms. The tensors are derived from the SONICOM HRTF Dataset (Engel et al., J. Audio Eng. Soc. 71(5), 2023, doi:10.17743/jaes.2022.0066). The SONICOM HRTFs are released under the MIT licence. This work develops research begun for the author’s B.Sc. dissertation at Birmingham City University.

items.summary: This technical note documents a conditional mathematical correspondence between the static spatial kernel used in conventional electromagnetic potential theory and the fixed-source gravitational potential in Lisa Doumbouya’s Harmonic Physics programme. Under supplied three-dimensional Euclidean geometry, spherical symmetry and stated boundary conditions, the derivation gives the static Green function 1/(4πr). Applying the existing gravitational source normalization yields the potential −μ/r, whose radial derivative gives the inward acceleration −μ/r². The note distinguishes potential, field amplitude, intensity, acceleration and optical measurement conversion, keeping geometric normalization separate from the distance exponent. The optical phase-ruler results are reviewed alongside the GRACE-FO forward forecasts. Calibrated reconstruction using measured phase retained micrometre-scale agreement with processed microwave ranging, while some forward models produced much larger errors. These results do not establish exponential error growth or identify a unique physical cause. The correspondence uses established mathematics and remains conditional on the supplied geometry, source calibration and physical interpretation. It does not establish an electromagnetic mechanism of gravity or derive spatial geometry from foundational Phase. The note includes the analytical proof, assumptions, evidence boundaries and requirements for a subsequent physical test. No new experimental data are introduced.

Numerical signal alignment alone cannot establish continuity of intention. Two systems may encode different signals while supporting the same functional command, or produce nearly identical latent representations while mapping to incompatible actions. The volume formulates meaning continuity as a conditional, falsifiable engineering and scientific hypothesis. It connects device-specific observation models, neural recording instability, task and action ontologies, paired old/new sensing periods, latent manifold bridging, longitudinal recalibration, calibrated abstention, functional validation, and an accessible right to reject the proposed migration. Its central commitment is that no amount of predictive accuracy can compensate for invalid authorization, an unverified physical reference, or loss of independent control. The research atlas comprises thirty connected mathematical derivations, eighty-two research chapters, and 410 independently paginated chapter sections that examine observables, inverse explanations, discriminating experiments, uncertainty and noncompensable safeguards, and independent requalification. Two hundred detailed Research Gates propose future falsification and handoff programs, while thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos preserve revisable candidate approaches rather than immutable conclusions. A claim-scoped DOI evidence ledger connects the study to published work on neural recording drift, decoder adaptation, manifold alignment, longitudinal neural interfaces, speech BCIs, user preferences, and neurotechnology ethics. The book is designed for both human researchers and future AI research systems. Its formulas, chapter cross-links, DOI anchors, competing models, negative-result requirements, and successor-focused research cards provide structured entry points for independent reconstruction and informed disagreement. The visual presentation combines ivory pages, navy and teal typography, and large gold mathematical plates, while mathematical expressions are also recorded in searchable source notation and a separate Excel reference index. This is a prospective, nonclinical research architecture. It does not report new patient experiments, demonstrate safe autonomous human neurovascular microrobots, establish a universal device-migration system, or claim continuity of private thoughts, consciousness, or personal identity. Scientific benefit remains conditional on explicit task definitions, qualified device evidence, legitimate permissions, external validation, and the successor's freedom to reject a failed bridge. Research question: What should remain invariant when an interface changes, and who has the authority to say that its meaning has changed?

items.summary: SELF-CALIBRATING NANO-NEURAL INTERFACES AND REFERENCE LINEAGE AT THE LIMIT Built-In References × Drift Attribution × Independent Functional Requalification STARLI / Institute XXIII / Research Flagship 17 PUBLICATION DESCRIPTION When a long-running neural interface changes, is the cause the sensor, the surrounding tissue, or the decoder? An adaptive algorithm can restore predictive accuracy while obscuring the physical origin of its own correction. This book proposes a rigorous, falsifiable architecture for self-calibrating nano-neural interfaces that must retain the scientific history of every reference and every update. Its central axiom is that self-calibration does not imply self-certification: measurement claims, permission to change, electrode safety and functional benefit demand independent evidence. The first coupling is the existence of physically traceable internal references that can be challenged against electrically and temporally independent standards. The second is a source-aware drift-diagnostic process that distinguishes electronics gain, electrode-tissue transfer, tissue-like surrogate changes, changing source signals and model/feature drift, explicitly recording instances of nonidentifiability. The third is external functional requalification, which can reject an apparently successful update after hidden-domain testing, material or reference replacement, loss of selectivity, missing raw observations, or inability to reproduce the frozen predecessor. This research monograph is divided into seven causal layers and 82 chapters. Five major subsections of each chapter are assigned independent pages, yielding 410 separately paginated technical essays. Thirty gold mathematical derivations are linked from chapter-opening equations to discriminating experiments. The mathematics includes augmented state-space observability, nonlinear observation functions, source-separation Jacobians, Kalman innovations, impedance spectroscopy, covariance propagation, change-point statistics, conformal coverage, selective risk, hard-veto constrained update eligibility, reference-bridge covariance, exact rollback and cross-laboratory requalification. A displayed formula is a candidate analytical instrument with stated dimensions and assumptions, not a discovered biological law. Two hundred detailed Research Gates are preserved at the rear: 82 interrogate source identifiability, another 82 challenge independent physical and evidential hard vetoes, and 36 require third-party reconstruction of a frozen reference history. Thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos propose revisable architectures, beginning with the Neural Interface Calibration Passport. The Passport ties an interface's physical identity to the raw analog and digitized record, calibrated unit chain, hardware reference ancestors, model and feature checksums, reasons for changing any reference, failed updates, revoked permissions, blinded requalification and rollback. These are proposed evidence structures, not commercially validated devices. The DOI bibliography contains 18 unique external research records covering chronic intracortical signal instability, low-dimensional BCI stabilization, decoder adaptation, long-term electrode-tissue behavior, complex impedance metrology, electrochemical reference limits, neural interface materials and conformal uncertainty under covariate shift. Selected publisher and PubMed pages were consulted for source metadata. Their findings cannot establish efficacy of the new self-calibration architecture; source-specific claims and independent replication would be necessary.

items.summary: This working paper develops a relational Phase interpretation of black holes within the Harmonic Physics research programme, using general relativity, exact Kerr geometry and semiclassical black-hole thermodynamics as its physical baseline. It examines how phase organisation, temporal reference, observer accessibility and information persistence might relate to black-hole closure. Within the proposed framework, a phase-cycle is a closed relational structure that supports recurrence. Measured succession requires distinguishable relations and persistent records, while geometry and causal history are treated as observer-level reconstructions. The temporal-anchor hypothesis concerns a deeper terminal condition at which the parent domain loses the internally usable references needed to resolve further clocks and geometry. This proposed condition is kept distinct from the regular event horizon, across which local evolution continues. Observation is described through a joint observation relation among admitted source organisation, a physical channel and an observer-capable organisation. Source state, coupling and registered record retain separate roles; changes in accessibility may alter registration while the source organisation persists. The paper consolidates three bounded mathematical findings: exact Kerr ingoing and outgoing endpoints can have opposite trapped and anti-trapped orientations with the same mass and spin parameters; spherical source/exterior matching leaves the transition law undetermined; and a leading slow-rotation calculation permits the same sign of angular momentum in closing and opening configurations. These results establish compatibility within the stated geometric constructions. A physical transition mechanism remains to be derived. Black-to-white-hole models provide external theoretical comparisons. Return to the original exterior and the opening of a daughter phase are treated as distinct hypotheses, each requiring an appropriate causal structure, state map and conservation accounting. The remaining requirements include an invariant parent-relative terminal criterion, a physical Phase-to-boundary map, transition dynamics, information and entropy accounting, and a stable nonperturbative rotating completion. The paper remains a developing theoretical interpretation supported by standard-geometry comparisons and bounded symbolic checks. It does not establish a physical black-to-white transition, information recovery through evaporation or a daughter universe. Version 2.3, dated 17 October 2026, updates observation and self-nesting terminology, clarifies geodesic incompleteness and fixed-angular-momentum assumptions, and refreshes the references. The existing displayed equations and reported test results are retained. keywords: Phase Theory; black holes; event horizons; geodesic incompleteness; relational time; phase contraction; information accessibility; singularity; white holes; quantum gravity.

items.summary: mm-ADL-Home is a cross-environment millimeter-wave radar point-cloud dataset for human activity recognition in furnished residential environments. The dataset was collected in four indoor environments comprising three simulated bachelor-unit layouts and one real bachelor unit, using the same activity taxonomy and radar configuration as the mm-ADL dataset (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22405011).  Each participant–environment recording is preserved as a continuous point-cloud stream and includes: (1) point_cloud.csv , containing radar point-cloud observations; (2) frame_labels.csv , containing frame-level activity annotations; (3) timestamps.csv , providing the temporal correspondence between radar and annotation frames; and (4) location_annotations.csv , containing the intervals used to register the radar sensor and landmark furniture in the radar coordinate system. The activity taxonomy covers locomotion, sitting and lying transitions, stationary sitting and lying, simulated falls, and floor-to-standing recovery. Location annotations identify sittable furniture, lieable furniture, kitchen locations, entry locations, and the radar sensor origin. These annotations support the reconstruction of room-level spatial context and furniture landmarks on the horizontal radar coordinate plane. The dataset contains complete recordings without a prescribed windowing or segmentation scheme, allowing users to implement their own preprocessing, temporal segmentation, domain adaptation, and evaluation protocols. Synchronized RGB recordings used during annotation are not included in the public release. Participant identifiers are pseudonymous.

items.summary: Data and analytical software for thermally activated Fe-SMA fibre-reinforced concrete This repository accompanies the article “Analytical modelling of thermally activated iron-based shape memory alloy fibre concrete: Finite transfer and capacity compatibility”. It provides the numerical source data, analytical implementation, calibration inputs, and results used to prepare the final article. The work examines finite fibre–matrix transfer, thermally activated composite response, cohesive-law identification, and the compatibility of reported strengths with uncertain fibre orientation and tensile capacity. The deposit contains one final analysis snapshot. It includes the reference formulation and the baselines, thermal alternatives, and cohesive-law candidates examined in the article. These are parts of the reported scientific assessment, rather than separate manuscript versions. Superseded model results, development archives, manuscript drafts, and unrelated source files are excluded. Contents • data/ contains numerical representations of published response curves, reported group statistics, study metadata, fixed constituent and pullout calibrations, optimizer initialization values, and published experimental/finite-element comparison curves. Curve identifiers preserve the link to the source study and figure. These are processed publication-based data, rather than original instrument records. • model/ contains the executable analysis scripts. items.summary: We develop a rigorous finite-dimensional mathematical framework connecting the renormalization group, gradient flows, Lyapunov stability, and noncooperative game theory. The central object is a renormalization-group flow written in gradient form, dg_i/dt = β_i(g) = - ∑_j G_ij(g) ∂Γ/∂g_j(g),          (1) where g = (g_1, …, g_n) belongs to an open domain M ⊂ ℝⁿ, Γ is a C² function, and G(g) is a symmetric positive-definite matrix. We associate to this flow a common-payoff game whose payoff is U(g) = - Γ(g).                   (2) We prove, with complete arguments, that ordinary Nash equilibria always imply renormalization-group fixed points, but the converse is false. We then identify the exact condition under which a fixed point becomes a genuine stable equilibrium of the game: a nondegenerate renormalization-group fixed point is asymptotically stable if and only if the Hessian of Γ is positive definite, if and only if it is a strict local minimum of Γ, if and only if it is a strict strong Nash equilibrium of U = -Γ. The distinction between ordinary Nash equilibrium and strong Nash equilibrium is essential. Ordinary Nash equilibria allow only unilateral deviations, while strong Nash equilibria exclude all small joint deviations. We provide explicit counterexamples showing that fixed points need not be Nash equilibria, that ordinary Nash equilibria need not be stable, and that invertibility of G alone does not imply finiteness of equilibria. We also prove global existence results under compactness and finiteness results under Morse nondegeneracy. The paper is self-contained at the level of multivariable calculus, linear algebra, ordinary differential equations, and basic Lyapunov stability theory. The framework is intentionally conditional: it does not claim that the gradient-flow representation has been proven in four-dimensional QCD or in any specific quantum field theory. Those issues are placed in a final section of open problems.
items.title: Gradient-Flow Renormalization Group as a Common-Potential Game: A Rigorous Equivalence Between Asymptotically Stable Fixed Points and Strict Strong Nash Equilibria

items.summary: This archive is provided as artifact material for the article "Synthesis and Verification of Register Automata over Data Sequences" for SETTA 2026. Abstract: Data sequences, such as time series, traces, and sensor streams, are words over large or infinite data domains. Their properties often depend on comparisons between values at different positions, which finite automata cannot express directly. We study synthesis and verification for Deterministic Register Automata (DRAs) over ordered data sequences. DRAs combine finite control with registers for remembered data values, providing compact symbolic descriptions of quantitative sequence languages. Our technical core is a local-search synthesis procedure and an exact robustness checker for DRAs. We fix the alphabet theory to ordered rationals $(\Q;<,=)$ with rational guard constants and use non-negative affine accumulator costs. For a fixed number of DRA registers, the checker runs in polynomial time; its dependence on that number is exponential. It reduces robustness to coverability and then to a shortest-path problem. Since the search ranges over $\Q^+$, it produces variable-length witnesses and, for RAA-definable alignment costs such as DTW, explores a counterexample space with no a priori length bound. As an application, we use learned DRAs as interpretable surrogates for queried neural sequence classifiers. A probably approximately correct (PAC) validation loop refines rejected candidates, returns genuine non-robustness witnesses for the classifier when found, and accepts a surrogate only with statistical guarantees for fidelity and local stability. We implement the framework in \textit{RAExc}, enabling the synthesis of interpretable automata and the verification of their robustness. We evaluate the approach on benchmark languages and sequentialized MNIST, demonstrating high accuracy while verifying the robustness of the learned automata.
items.title: Synthesis and Verification of Transformer Programs

items.summary: Coding agents can now interpret a specification, implement it, write and execute tests, repair failures, and declare the result ready for release. When the same agentic system produces both the software and the evidence of its correctness, a passing test suite no longer constitutes independent evidence. Visible tests become an optimization target, and code, tests, and oracles may share a single misinterpretation of the specification. This paper argues that agent-produced software requires an assurance plane that is structurally independent of the build plane. We first characterize four gaps along the chain from stakeholder intent to production, namely the requirement, conformance, evaluation, and model gaps, and identify which of them verification can close. We then propose a framework that separates building from verifying, introduces a Verification Contract stating what must be demonstrated before release, and organizes verification in two phases: a specification-first phase designed without access to the implementation, and an implementation-aware phase that strengthens the evidence through mutation analysis, property-based testing, and fuzzing. The resulting evidence is consolidated into an assurance report that makes residual uncertainty explicit and leaves the release decision to a human. We evaluate the framework in a pre-registered study on three stateful services, two of them written by third-party models, and an EvalPlus pilot, comparing self-validation with independent verification under context-level and model-level independence. The builder's programs were correct, but its own tests missed subtle interactions: a verifier in a fresh context detected more of the 46 seeded faults than the builder's tests (Holm-corrected p = 0.006), and surfaced the ambiguities of the specification, at the price of rare false oracles. A verifier from another provider did not add detection. The framework and the study provide a basis for governing the release of software produced by agents.
items.title: Who Verifies the Builder? Toward Independent Assurance for Agent-Produced Software

items.summary: The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 allows a child aged sixteen or seventeen who is alleged to have committed a heinous offence to be tried as an adult after a "preliminary assessment" by the Juvenile Justice Board. This paper argues that the transfer mechanism is less a principled answer to serious adolescent offending than a legislative compromise whose costs fall on the procedural guarantees the Act otherwise extends to children. It reads section 15 against the Supreme Court's decisions in Shilpa Mittal and Barun Chandra Thakur, the age-determination case law, and the developmental research on adolescent culpability, and it engages the retributive and victim-centred case for transfer on its own terms. Accountability and rehabilitation, the paper contends, are not two poles to be traded off at a single age threshold. Both depend on institutional capacity that the system has never been resourced to supply: functioning Boards, trained probation staff, individual care plans that are actually followed, and aftercare that reaches young people beyond eighteen. Reform should narrow and proceduralise transfer, introduce statutory diversion, decouple offence classification from the general penal code, and treat implementation failure as a rights violation rather than an administrative shortfall.
items.title: Reforming Juvenile Justice in India: Balancing Child Rights, Accountability, and Rehabilitation

( Under Review ) ABSTRACT Alluvial meanders dynamically adjust their planform and channel geometry, yet classical meander theory assumes a spatially uniform, constant channel width and continuous bank retreat, failing to capture episodic bank collapse and non-uniform width adjustments in transitional meandering rivers. Situated along the geomorphic continuum between single-thread and wandering streams, transitional meanders exhibit pronounced spatial width variations that break cross-sectional symmetry. Here, we develop a physically closed, reduced-complexity morphodynamic framework coupling a three-parameter asymptotic expansion of the three-dimensional Reynolds-averaged flow equations, continuous basal toe scour with transient pore-water suction, threshold-governed cantilever limit equilibrium, and a mass-conserving sediment partition driving inner point-bar progradation. The formulation demonstrates that the spatial phase relationship between channel width oscillations and centerline curvature steers the spatial displacement of outer-bank shear stress hotspots: channel constriction upstream of the bend apex amplifies cutbank shear stress, whereas channel expansion decelerates flow and promotes point-bar accretion. Discrete slump-block deposits provide self-adaptive hydraulic shielding that stabilizes the toe and regulates decadal channel relaxation. Hindcasting the 40-year morphodynamic evolution of the transitional Powder River, Montana, across 34 monumented cross sections reproduces post-flood channel widening and subsequent multi-decadal recovery narrowing across 228 discrete collapse events, while in the limit of uniform width the model recovers classical constant-width meander theory with first-order convergence along the meandering Juruá River. items.summary: The Voynich Manuscript exhibits strong statistical regularities, but the distinction between recoverable grammar and recoverable lexical meaning remains unresolved. This study asks how far a progressively frozen, cross-validated analysis can reconstruct the manuscript’s internal word-building system without assigning meanings from illustrations, candidate languages, or post-hoc English paraphrase. Using canonical transcription, protected holdout partitions, alternate-transcription replication, exact host substitutions, and adversarial stopping rules, the analysis recovers a cumulative left-edge morphology, a transferable inventory of 39 surface CORE-0 stem/bodies, reproducible host-by-right-state coupling, a stable K/T referential contrast, and a directed network among powered lexical cores. The 39-core inventory predicts protected-frame combinatorics and content-blind contextual fingerprints out of sample, while attempts to decompose these bodies into a deeper transferable root layer fail. Nine recurring hosts show strongly replicated coupling to EY/EEY/EDY right-edge states, supporting a distributed morphological paradigm rather than independent left- and right-side systems. A 28-node directed CORE network also replicates across canonical calibration, untouched Holdout, and alternate-transcription tests, yielding neutral outbound- and inbound-biased stem classes without requiring part-of-speech or semantic assignments. On the project’s fully constrained 1,609-line benchmark, 12,299 of 12,495 positions are role-naturalizable (98.4314%), leaving 196 opaque positions. This percentage is explicitly a conditional benchmark-maturity statistic, not a measure of literal plaintext recovery or manuscript-wide translation accuracy. Repeated attempts to cross from structural organization to ordinary lexical meaning—including deeper-root induction, topic clustering, functional-neighborhood anchoring, local lexical syntax, illustration matching, source-language fitting, and prospective semantic transfer—fail the project’s promotion criteria. The resulting contribution is therefore a structural decipherment rather than a lexical one: a reproducible grammatical and morphological architecture together with an empirically identified lexical-identifiability ceiling. The work extends, but is distinct from, the earlier controlled-translation release at DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22049207.

items.summary: Image harmonization methods adjust the colour and lighting of an object pasted into a photograph so that it looks native to its new scene, and they are ranked by average error on one benchmark whose test images are real photographs with one object recoloured. One photograph can yield several such test images, and the benchmark promises that no photograph appears in both the training and the test split. We find that 1,399 photographs do, and the composites built on them are a quarter of the test set. Duplicate checks over file names or bytes miss this, because every composite is a different file. On that quarter the three methods we score end to end read two to five times lower error than on the rest, but most of the gap is composition rather than the sharing: the shared composites come almost entirely from one of the benchmark's four source collections, and inside that collection the gap falls to about one and a half times. An official score is therefore an average over two populations, mixed in a proportion the benchmark does not report. We release a test list of 5,581 composites whose construction identities do not appear in training, with four near-duplicate pairs disclosed rather than removed, adoptable without retraining at the price of one rescore per checkpoint. We leave open whether the sharing itself changes what a model learns. Contents of this record. The paper, the supplement, the LaTeX source of both, the record metadata and the licence statement. The identity matcher, the composite-locality and sensitivity checks, the CPU tests, the official iHarmony4 lists and the corrected test list are released under the MIT license at https://github.com/Buljic/only-means-only . What this record does not contain. No dataset, no images, no masks, no model checkpoints and no third-party baseline code or weights; those are described and cited by the paper and remain under their own terms. This is a preprint. items.summary: This report establishes an exact conditional mathematical correspondence between a specified two-component phase model and the sine-Gordon equation appearing in a classical string-theory reduction. Developed within the Harmonic Physics Research Programme, the model uses interacting phase components labelled expansion and contraction in the proposed physical interpretation. For a continuum action with a cosine interaction, constant coefficients and equal component propagation speeds, an invertible change of variables separates the dynamics into an exact nonlinear sine-Gordon equation for the normalized relative phase and a free wave equation for the common phase. The interaction potential can also be expressed through the squared magnitude of the difference between two complex phase components. The derivation retains the full nonlinearity, extending the correspondence beyond the small-angle approximation. Direct numerical evolution of the original component fields provides a reproducible check at finite relative-phase amplitude. The reported breather benchmark reaches a peak relative-phase excursion of approximately 2.574 radians, with a maximum sampled error of approximately 6.3 × 10⁻⁹ radians over two oscillation periods. Component amplitudes remain fixed. Interaction-removal and unequal-speed controls document the failure to recover the same target when the specified conditions are changed. The string-theory connection is examined through the Pohlmeyer reduction of classical strings on R_t × S². A separate conventional kink embedding is checked against the local geometric constraints and string equations of motion. The evolved phase breather is not reconstructed as a string. The established result is a conditional correspondence between reduced classical equations; a full physical or quantum equivalence between the proposed phase model and string theory remains unestablished. Version 1.0 includes the standalone report and an accompanying reproducibility archive containing mathematical derivations, executable Python scripts, numerical settings, sampled synthetic data, control results, figures, source provenance, checksum manifests and reproduction instructions. A documented replay of the retained calculation and an AI-assisted computational audit support inspection and reuse of the reported results. items.summary: This archive is provided as artifact material for the article "Synthesis and Verification of Register Automata over Data Sequences" for SETTA 2026. Abstract: Data sequences, such as time series, traces, and sensor streams, are words over large or infinite data domains. Their properties often depend on comparisons between values at different positions, which finite automata cannot express directly. We study synthesis and verification for Deterministic Register Automata (DRAs) over ordered data sequences. DRAs combine finite control with registers for remembered data values, providing compact symbolic descriptions of quantitative sequence languages. Our technical core is a local-search synthesis procedure and an exact robustness checker for DRAs. We fix the alphabet theory to ordered rationals $(\Q;<,=)$ with rational guard constants and use non-negative affine accumulator costs. For a fixed number of DRA registers, the checker runs in polynomial time; its dependence on that number is exponential. It reduces robustness to coverability and then to a shortest-path problem. Since the search ranges over $\Q^+$, it produces variable-length witnesses and, for RAA-definable alignment costs such as DTW, explores a counterexample space with no a priori length bound. As an application, we use learned DRAs as interpretable surrogates for queried neural sequence classifiers. A probably approximately correct (PAC) validation loop refines rejected candidates, returns genuine non-robustness witnesses for the classifier when found, and accepts a surrogate only with statistical guarantees for fidelity and local stability. We implement the framework in \textit{RAExc}, enabling the synthesis of interpretable automata and the verification of their robustness. We evaluate the approach on benchmark languages and sequentialized MNIST, demonstrating high accuracy while verifying the robustness of the learned automata.
items.title: Synthesis and Verification of Transformer Programs

items.summary: Decentralized multi-robot shape formation in GPS-denied environments is important for search-and-rescue and disaster response. Conventional consensus-based formation controllers can violate safe separation, oscillate, or stall when communication degrades, sensors are noisy, or an agent drops out. This paper proposes a resilient decentralized controller that combines Huber-weighted consensus and Exponential Moving Average (EMA) state estimation with a Dual-Layer Artificial Potential Field (APF) safety barrier. The first layer adds an anti-symmetric lateral deflection to resolve head-on encounters between peers; the second applies a normal-plus-tangential circulation field around static obstacles. The framework is evaluated on five simulated nonholonomic differential-drive robots in Gazebo Harmonic (ROS 2 Jazzy). Three runs are compared: a linear consensus baseline, the same baseline under faults (15% packet loss, 50-150 ms delay, σ = 0.18 m sensor noise, and a mid-run agent blackout), and the proposed controller under the same faults. The fault-free baseline reached the pentagon fastest (0.0156 m final RMS error) but its minimum separation fell to 0.3918 m, with 31 logged violations of the 0.50 m margin. Under faults the baseline reached 0.0546 m with 5 violations (minimum 0.4833 m). The proposed controller recorded no violations, kept a minimum separation of 0.6757 m, and reached 0.0368 m final error, at the cost of slower convergence (about 21 s versus about 12-15 s). Results are from single simulation runs, and the safety barrier is empirical rather than formally guaranteed.
items.title: Resilient Decentralized Shape Formation of Multi-Robot Swarms Under Adversarial Real-World Faults in High-Complexity Disaster Environments

items.summary: Large language models often penalize multilingual users through hidden 'tokenizer taxes' caused by subword fragmentation. Geographic proper nouns offer a controlled stress case for this distributional asymmetry, as they are standardized, cross-linguistically available entities whose orthographic forms frequently mismatch tokenizer training distributions. We introduce the Cross-Linguistic Orthographic Uniqueness Score (CLOUS), a character-level metric based on Shannon surprisal that quantifies the orthographic rarity of localized country names. We evaluate CLOUS on a controlled corpus of 249 ISO-registered country names; generalization to other geographic entity types remains future work. We evaluate CLOUS against tokenization fertility for six production tokenizers spanning three algorithm families across eleven languages and seven script families. Using Spearman rank correlation with Benjamini-Hochberg correction, CLOUS shows significant associative strength with fertility in 61 of 65 valid language-tokenizer combinations. As a screening tool for high-fragmentation entities, CLOUS achieves ROC-AUC = 0.850 and F1 = 0.740, correctly identifying approximately three-quarters of the highest-fragmentation entities from orthographic properties alone. We further show that CLOUS correlates with fertility more strongly than length-based baselines across all evaluated scripts, and outperforms a character bigram surprisal model in 69.2% of tested combinations, particularly for logographic, syllabic, and Latin scripts. Conversely, the bigram baseline proves superior for morphophonologically complex scripts like Arabic and Devanagari, indicating that tokenizer fragmentation is driven by local orthographic context in some scripts and absolute character rarity in others. Script family appears to be the primary driver of CLOUS-fertility correlation strength, with effect sizes ranging from modest for Latin-script languages ) to large for non-Latin scripts (   up to 0.686 for Japanese). These findings suggest that CLOUS may be useful as a lightweight pre-tokenization diagnostic for multilingual NLP pipelines.
items.title: Estimating Cross-Lingual Tokenization Fragmentation Risk: A Frequency-Based Uniqueness Score for Geographic Entities

items.summary: Version 2.0 is a substantive revision of version 1.0 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19174862). It supersedes the earlier procedural interpretation and its exclusion of competing explanations. The revised title is Structural Organization and Interpretive Limits of the Phaistos Disc. Reproduced descriptive findings are retained; failed model comparisons and photographic uncertainties are reported explicitly. The earlier version remains available through the record version history. We examine whether reproducible structural observations on the Phaistos Disc support a procedural interpretation. A pinned numerical transcription contains 242 main-sign positions, including one unreadable position, 45 readable sign types, 61 divider-defined groups and 18 supplementary stroke annotations. Source review reconciles counting and numbering conventions while retaining unresolved photographic uncertainty. The 02-to-12 side contrast persists after exact-family collapse. Adding side to a fixed position-only pairing predictor improves held-family loss by 0.082738 nats, but its exact conditional tail of 0.075 fails the frozen support rule. A positional mixture fails to outperform a bigram baseline. A separate directional test of the proposed 07-to-27 recovery relationship fails, with a one-sided permutation tail of 0.884. items.summary: Research compendium for the article "Climate warming is projected to reduce and redistribute Aedes albopictus abundance, away from Po Valley hotspots towards Alpine margins" (M. C. The study predicts weekly ovitrap egg counts of the Asian tiger mosquito at 149 monitoring stations in Italy, Albania, Switzerland and France (VectAbundance, 2010–2022). items.summary: The following dataset contains images and band count estimates of shortfin mako ( Isurus oxyrinchus ) vertebrae. It is intended to assist with the replication of the results for the study: Automated reading of vertebral images for aging shortfin mako ( Isurus oxyrinchus ) using Bayesian deep learning. Samples were obtained from two primary sources: recreational game fishing competitions primarily from the North Island between 1994 and 2003, and through the Ministry for Primary Industries (MPI) Fisheries Observer Programme between 2002 and 2003, primarily from the South Island (Bishop et al., 2006). Shortfin mako vertebrae images (n=146, belonging to 131 unique sharks) were obtained from previous ageing studies using band counts (Bishop et al., 2006; Francis, 2016). Most vertebrae images were of half bow-tie section pairs. These section pairs were filtered by image quality with lower quality images being excluded, resulting in a reduced dataset of 133 section pairs. Each section pair was isolated, resulting in a complete dataset of 266 half bow-tie section images. We compared the following three deep learning methods: DeepEnsembling, a mixture of Laplace approximations, and multi-stochastic weight average Gaussian to predict the band counts by human readers using a dataset of 146 images of shortfin mako ( Isurus oxyrinchus ) vertebrae. Multi-stochastic weight average Gaussian offered marginally superior predictive power and uncertainty calibration, and its predictions typically matched estimates provided by human readers. We conclude that the application of deep learning for automated vertebrae reading demonstrated strong initial promise.
items.title: Vertebral section images for shortfin mako (Isurus oxyrinchus)

items.summary: LONGITUDINAL DEVICE MIGRATION AND MEANING CONTINUITY AT THE LIMIT Device Replacement × Model Bridging × Control Semantics STARLI RESEARCH WORKS | INSTITUTE XXIV | FLAGSHIP 24 Feng Cheng-en 33 × Starli Research Works This research monograph investigates a deceptively difficult question in long-term brain–computer interfaces: when sensors, acquisition electronics, firmware, electrode geometry, or decoding models change, what would justify the claim that a user's task-grounded control meaning has been preserved? Numerical signal alignment alone cannot establish continuity of intention. Two systems may encode different signals while supporting the same functional command, or produce nearly identical latent representations while mapping to incompatible actions. The volume formulates meaning continuity as a conditional, falsifiable engineering and scientific hypothesis. It connects device-specific observation models, neural recording instability, task and action ontologies, paired old/new sensing periods, latent manifold bridging, longitudinal recalibration, calibrated abstention, functional validation, and an accessible right to reject the proposed migration. Its central commitment is that no amount of predictive accuracy can compensate for invalid authorization, an unverified physical reference, or loss of independent control. The research atlas comprises thirty connected mathematical derivations, eighty-two research chapters, and 410 independently paginated chapter sections that examine observables, inverse explanations, discriminating experiments, uncertainty and noncompensable safeguards, and independent requalification. Two hundred detailed Research Gates propose future falsification and handoff programs, while thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos preserve revisable candidate approaches rather than immutable conclusions. The book is designed for both human researchers and future AI research systems. Its formulas, chapter cross-links, DOI anchors, competing models, negative-result requirements, and successor-focused research cards provide structured entry points for independent reconstruction and informed disagreement. The visual presentation combines ivory pages, navy and teal typography, and large gold mathematical plates, while mathematical expressions are also recorded in searchable source notation and a separate Excel reference index. This is a prospective, nonclinical research architecture. It does not report new patient experiments, demonstrate safe autonomous human neurovascular microrobots, establish a universal device-migration system, or claim continuity of private thoughts, consciousness, or personal identity. items.summary: Description This dataset accompanies a comparative evolutionary-genomics study of ancestral cytosine substitution patterns across human, chimpanzee, bonobo and gorilla lineages. Using hg38-centered UCSC multiz primate alignments and a seven-species phylogenetic framework, we reconstructed ancestral nucleotide states and quantified cytosine substitutions across all 22 human autosomes. The analysis examined CG, CHG and CHH sequence contexts, 256 strand-canonicalized ancestral 5-mer motifs, and lineage-specific substitution patterns. The deposited files include: Chromosome-level ancestral-site datasets at a minimum ancestral-state posterior probability of 0.95. Chromosome-specific 5-mer substitution summaries and quality-control records. Genome-wide cytosine substitution frequencies and context-enrichment ratios. Chromosome-bootstrap uncertainty estimates and cross-lineage motif comparisons. Statistical analyses of lineage-specific motif deviations, including simultaneous confidence intervals. Leave-one-autosome-out predictive comparisons of ancestral 3-mer and 5-mer sequence context. Frozen methodology documentation, validation records, checksums and the fixed seven-species phylogenetic tree. The dataset supports independent examination and downstream reanalysis of the reported numerical findings. Data provenance: UCSC Genome Browser hg38-centered 30-primate multiz alignments, restricted to seven primate species. Computational methods: IQ-TREE 2.3.6 ancestral-state reconstruction under GTR+F+G4, followed by custom Python-based sequence-context and statistical analyses. items.summary: Discrete audio tokenization has become the critical interface between raw waveforms and autoregressive modeling in recent music generation. As a result, music tokenizers must simultaneously support high-fidelity reconstruction and produce discrete sequences that remain amenable to language modeling. Existing reconstruction-oriented tokenizers often mix musical structure with fine acoustic details, producing high-entropy tokens that are hard to model. In contrast, semantics-guided alternatives are designed for speech and do not fit music well, often hurting reconstruction quality. We address these trade-offs by rethinking music tokenization around a measurable notion of music semantic content grounded in downstream Music Information Retrieval tasks. Guided by this definition, we propose MuSeC, a music semantic codec that factorizes semantic and acoustic content directly from mixed signals without source separation. MuSeC preserves information required for high-fidelity reconstruction while producing more LM-friendly discrete units. Empirically, it improves reconstruction quality and yields more predictable token sequences, providing a practical foundation toward high-fidelity LLM music generation. Demos are available at https://longwaytog0.github.io/MuSeC/.
items.title: Rethinking Music Tokenization: A Semantic Codec toward High-Fidelity LLM Music Generation

items.summary: Automatic Drum Transcription (ADT) is commonly formulated as a direct mapping from a music mixture to symbolic drum events. While effective for transcription, this formulation discards the acoustic stems that are useful for editing, remixing, and production. We revisit an alternative separate-and-detect formulation, where a drum source separation front end first produces five editable drum stems, and a fixed onset detector then converts each stem into symbolic events. The separator is built on a five-stem latent diffusion model that jointly generates kick, snare, toms, hi-hats, and cymbals in a compact VAE latent space. We further study two training-only auxiliary branches--an onset branch (OB) and a timbre branch (TB)--which shape the separator during learning but are discarded at inference. Trained on synthetic drum multitracks and evaluated on MDB Drums and ENST-Drums, the proposed pipeline consistently improves over a strong U-Net-based drum separation baseline in overall transcription F1. It also outperforms a representative end-to-end ADT system on kick and snare F1 under our evaluation protocol, while additionally providing separated audio stems. The ablation results show that OB gives the most stable transcription gains, whereas TB changes the trade-off between reconstruction, acoustic stem quality, and onset detection. These results suggest that generative drum demixing can serve not only as a source separation model, but also as a practical front end for interpretable drum transcription.
items.title: Separate-and-Detect: Unified Drum Transcription and Stem Generation via Latent Diffusion

items.summary: Hashing, signing, and timestamping establish that a document has not changed. When a legal document is produced by composition, from templates, clause libraries, shared definitions, and parameters that evolve independently, the governing text is a resolved state, and the integrity of the root document does not ensure that this state can be reconstructed. We treat this as a problem of ex post auditability. We define the resolved state as S_t = ρ(A_0, R_t, C_t), derive five properties of its auditability from requirements established in archival science, legal document standards, and norm-change formalisms, and introduce a capture model K_t with a diagnostic procedure that reports which properties a capture fails. We implement the framework in cmacc-attest and apply it to the 175 instantiated contracts of the CommonAccord library. References resolve in 96.6% of contracts, yet none is auditable: no reference is version-locked, and 98.3% contain conflicts settled by an unattested precedence order. Replaying 194 commits of the library history shows that 88.5% of the changes in resolved contracts left the root file unchanged. Repository history narrows reconstruction when the time of resolution is known, but does not replace a capture.
items.title: Beyond Document Integrity: Auditing Resolved States of Formalized Legal Documents

items.summary: This replication package accompanies the paper "An Exploratory Evaluation of Targeted Label Poisoning in a Client-Local Feature Federated Ensemble for Chest X-Ray Classification." It contains code and saved experimental results for an exploratory study of Pneumonia-to-Normal label poisoning in four-class chest X-ray classification. The study uses 20,795 images from three public sources, with 20,557 perceptual groups kept intact across experimental partitions. The package covers 212 completed training jobs, including main and component comparisons, classifier-head sensitivity, image-model references, candidate probability banks, and earlier-poisoning experiments. The main comparisons and image-model references use ten deterministic seeds. The classifier-head and GRU-structure study uses three seeds. Included materials comprise dataset manifests and image checksums, perceptual-group metadata, split assignments, seeds and configurations, held-out predictions, candidate probabilities, numerical summaries, result figures, analysis and verification scripts, and scientific execution-source snapshots. Additional fixed-model analyses examine validation availability, validation-label contamination, and artifact retention. The README and reproducibility guide explain verification, reanalysis, environment requirements, and dataset reconstruction. Dataset images and model checkpoints are not included. Obtain the source images separately under their applicable access and use terms: COVID-19 Radiography Database: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/tawsifurrahman/covid19-radiography-database COVID19, Pneumonia, Normal Chest X-ray Images: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/sachinkumar413/covid-pneumonia-normal-chest-xray-images Tuberculosis Chest X-ray Dataset: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/tawsifurrahman/tuberculosis-tb-chest-xray-dataset The included metadata identify the exact study images for reconstruction from the original source bytes. Saved results can be checked without source images or retraining. The attack direction was selected exploratorily, perceptual grouping does not establish patient independence, and source-held-out generalization was not evaluated. Reuse rights are described in LICENSE_STATUS.txt. This work was supported by the Deanship of Scientific Research (DSR) at King Abdulaziz University, Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, under grant No. IPP: 455-611-2026.
items.title: Replication Package for: An Exploratory Evaluation of Targeted Label Poisoning in a Client-Local Feature Federated Ensemble for Chest X-Ray Classification

items.summary: Four-dimensional beam-matrix reconstruction from quadrupole scans is the standard way to mea- sure cross-plane coupling and the intrinsic emittances that a decoupling section can recover. We show that a scan of a single thin quadrupole, normal or skew and placed anywhere in a linear lattice, determines at most nine of the ten beam-matrix parameters for any number of settings, because each measured second moment is quadratic in the quadrupole strength. The unmeasured direction lies in the x–y cross block and has a closed form in terms of the transfer matrices; for a quadrupole followed by a drift of length L its nonzero entries are Wxpy = Wpxy = 1 and Wpxpy = −2/L. Both projected emittances are therefore measured, but the beam matrices consistent with the data form a line segment along which the smaller intrinsic emittance ranges from zero to slightly above its true value, so a single-knob scan gives only an upper bound on it. A thick quadrupole restores the miss- ing direction only weakly, its singular value scaling approximately as the sixth power of the magnet length. Scanning two independently powered quadrupoles of any type makes the reconstruction well posed without additional hardware.
items.title: Single-knob quadrupole scans do not determine the intrinsic emittances
